subject: Math
prompt: Which expression is equivalent to $(5x(x-5) - 3(x-5))/(4x-20)$, where $x > 5$ ?
explanation: Choice B is correct. The numerator $5x(x-5) - 3(x-5)$ contains a common factor of $(x-5)$ in both terms. Factoring out $(x-5)$ gives $(x-5)(5x-3)$. The denominator $4x-20$ can be factored as $4(x-5)$. The expression becomes $\frac{(x-5)(5x-3)}{4(x-5)}$. Since $x > 5$, the factor $(x-5)$ is nonzero and can be canceled, yielding $\frac{5x-3}{4}$.
